summary: Cameron Park sits on the western slope of the Sierra Nevada foothills at roughly 1,200–1,600 feet of elevation, which means summer highs regularly push past 90°F while winter nights dip into the upper 30s — an annual average of 72°F daytime high and 9.3 hours of sunshine per day creates a landscape of golden grass, scattered oaks, and genuinely dramatic sunsets over the Sacramento Valley below. This is a bedroom community in the truest sense: the local economy lacks a major employment center, and most working residents commute west on U.S. Route 50 toward Folsom, Rancho Cordova, or Sacramento — a corridor that can turn a 30-mile drive into 60-plus minutes during peak hours. At a median household income of roughly $98,000 against a median home value of $641,100, the price-to-income ratio lands around 6.6×, which is steep but notably lower than much of the Sacramento metro's closer-in suburbs. The terrain itself is the defining feature: rolling granite hills, ravines thick with live oak and manzanita, and pocket neighborhoods connected more by winding roads than sidewalks — Cameron Park Lake offers a small recreational anchor, but daily errands almost always involve a car. With about 17,300 residents spread across 11.3 square miles and a density of just 1,530 per square mile, it reads more as semi-rural foothill living than conventional suburb — the tradeoff is unmistakable: space and quiet bought with windshield time.
